_why: The channel's lineup, one table read by the station (mac/station.py, which hands the writer the show's tone) and by the page (the schedule, on now, the shows). Hours are Chiang Mai time, fractional (12.25 is 12:15). The first show whose hours hold the time wins, so short shows sit before the long ones they air inside (PNN's way, 8 Oct 2026). A short show with a kind does every middle part of a run as that kind. Tone lines stay one sentence: the 8 Oct lab found longer direction bought nothing on Haiku.

shows.name: Try It On
shows.blurb: Fifteen minutes of March living one idea out loud.
shows.tone: A short morning show: March tries the idea on herself as if it were her morning, and the narrator coaches.

shows.name: Quick Fire
shows.blurb: Fifteen minutes, nothing over ten words.
shows.tone: A short lunchtime show: fast, light and funny, no speeches.

shows.name: The Case Against
shows.blurb: One note on trial. Somebody has to defend it.
shows.tone: A short afternoon show: a trial of one idea, played half like a courtroom.

shows.name: Legends
shows.blurb: The narrator reads one note as an old legend.
shows.tone: A short evening show: the narrator's own slot, told from an old book, with March heckling.

shows.name: The Long Night
shows.blurb: The graveyard shift. Slower, quieter, bigger.
shows.tone: The small hours: slower and quieter, the narrator tells it big and March lets him, mostly.

shows.name: The Morning Desk
shows.blurb: Every idea brought down to an ordinary morning.
shows.tone: Morning: March pulls every idea down to the first hour of an ordinary day.

shows.name: The Main Desk
shows.tone: The daytime show: the regular rundown, sharp and even.

shows.name: The Epic
shows.blurb: Prime time. His notebook, told as a chapter of an epic.
shows.tone: Prime time: the narrator tells the note as a chapter of an epic, and March is the one keeping it honest.

shows.name: The Late Edition
shows.blurb: Late, looser, a little more honest.
shows.tone: Late night: looser and more honest; if a sincere moment is due, it fits best here.
